blocks.text: Practice long questions for the whole of Chapter 6 (Emerging Technologies), in the shape of a Board long question: each theory question carries 8 marks (define, explain with examples, compare, write and explain a program), often as a definition plus explained points (e.g. 2 + 3 x 2). Each question has a full model answer.

blocks.prompt: 1 Emerging technologies are changing the way we live and work. (i) Define emerging technologies. (ii) Explain Artificial Intelligence, the Internet of Things and Quantum Computing with one example or use each. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Definition: Emerging technologies are new tools, systems and methods that are currently being developed or have just started to be used. They have the potential to change the way we live, work and interact with the world.

(ii) 1. Artificial Intelligence (AI): AI refers to machines and software that can think and learn like humans. It can help with tasks like recognizing faces, understanding speech and making decisions. Example: it is used in everything from smart assistants like Siri to self-driving cars.

2. Internet of Things (IoT): IoT connects everyday objects, like refrigerators, cars and even clothes, to the internet. This allows them to send and receive data, making our lives more convenient. Example: a smart thermostat can learn your schedule and adjust the temperature in your home automatically.

3. Quantum Computing: Quantum computers use the principles of quantum physics to process information much faster than traditional computers. They have the potential to solve very complex problems that are currently impossible for regular computers to handle.

book_ref.quote: Here are some of the key emerging technologies

blocks.prompt: 2 Explain the following emerging technologies, giving the use or example of each from the book: Augmented Reality, Virtual Reality, 5G Technology and Biotechnology. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
1. Augmented Reality (AR): AR adds digital elements to the real world using devices like smartphones or glasses. It is used in gaming, education and training.

2. Virtual Reality (VR): VR creates a completely virtual environment that you can interact with using special equipment. Like AR, it is used in gaming, education and training.

3. 5G Technology: 5G is the next generation of wireless technology, offering much faster internet speeds and more reliable connections. This will enable better performance for mobile phones, smart devices and even new technologies like AR and VR.

4. Biotechnology: Biotechnology involves using living organisms, like bacteria and plants, to create new products or solve problems. For example, scientists use biotechnology to develop new medicines, improve crops and even create environmentally friendly materials.

book_ref.quote: These technologies are used in gaming, education, and training

blocks.prompt: 3 Cloud computing rests on a few basic concepts. (i) Define cloud computing. (ii) Explain virtualization, scalability with elasticity, and on-demand access, giving the book's example of each. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Definition: Cloud computing is a model that allows easy and convenient access to computing resources like servers, storage and applications over the internet. These resources can be quickly provided and released with minimal management effort or service provider interaction. You only pay for what you use; it is like renting a supercomputer that you can use whenever you need it, from anywhere in the world.

(ii) 1. Virtualization: a technology that allows a single physical machine to run multiple virtual machines. Each virtual computer runs its own operating system and applications as if it were an independent machine. This makes better use of the hardware, reduces costs and allows easier management and flexibility: it turns one computer into many.

2. Scalability and elasticity: scalability means you can add more resources when you need them. Example: an online store gets a huge spike in traffic during Eid or 14th August sales and adds more servers so the website does not slow down or crash. Elasticity goes a step further: the system automatically adjusts resources based on current demand, adding servers when traffic rises and reducing them after the sale, so you do not pay for resources you don't need.

3. On-demand access: you can use computing resources whenever you need them, without waiting for a long setup process, like turning on a tap instead of digging a well. Example: a student who suddenly needs extra storage for a school project can instantly rent it from a cloud provider and start using it right away.

book_ref.quote: Cloud computing is like having a powerful computer that you can access over the internet

blocks.prompt: 4 A college has three needs: renting virtual servers on which its staff install their own operating system and software, giving student developers a ready environment to build and deploy an app, and giving every teacher email and online documents. Which type of cloud service suits each need? Explain each type with the book's examples. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
Cloud services are categorized into three main types (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS), each offering different levels of control, flexibility and management.

1. Renting virtual servers: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS). IaaS offers basic computing infrastructure such as servers, storage and networking on a pay-as-you-go basis. Users have control over the operating systems, applications and storage, but not the underlying physical infrastructure, so the staff can install their own operating system and software. Examples: Amazon Web Services (AWS) lets users rent virtual servers; Microsoft Azure and Google Compute Engine are other IaaS providers.

2. Environment to build and deploy an app: Platform as a Service (PaaS). PaaS offers a complete development and deployment environment in the cloud: infrastructure (servers, storage, networking), middleware, development tools and management services. Developers focus on coding and deploying without managing hardware and software layers. Examples: Google App Engine, Microsoft Azure App Services and Heroku.

3. Email and online documents: Software as a Service (SaaS). SaaS provides access to software applications hosted and managed by the service provider; users simply subscribe and use them over the internet. It is convenient because it needs no hardware management or software updates. Examples: Google Workspace (Gmail, Google Docs, Google Drive), Microsoft Office 365 and Salesforce.

book_ref.quote: There are different types of cloud services that cater to various needs

blocks.prompt: 5 Suggest a suitable cloud deployment model for each case and justify it from the book: a large bank holding sensitive customer data; a company that needs everyday operations cheaply but must keep critical data secure during busy periods; a company that cannot afford to stop if one cloud provider has problems; a small business that wants low-cost computing resources without managing hardware. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
Cloud deployment models define how cloud services are made available and used; each offers different levels of control, security and flexibility.

1. Large bank: Private cloud. A private cloud is used exclusively by one organization and is not shared; it can be hosted in the bank's own data centers or by a third-party provider, but only the bank has access to it. Private clouds are more secure but expensive, which suits sensitive customer data.

2. Everyday operations plus secure critical data: Hybrid cloud. A hybrid cloud combines public and private clouds, allowing data and applications to be shared between them. The company uses the public cloud for everyday operations and the private cloud for sensitive data; during busy periods it moves less sensitive data and applications to the public cloud while keeping critical data in the private cloud. Hybrid clouds offer flexibility and control.

3. Cannot stop if one provider fails: Multi-cloud. It uses multiple cloud services from different providers (e.g. Google Cloud Platform for analytics, Microsoft Azure for enterprise applications, AWS for backup and disaster recovery). It avoids dependency on a single provider; if one provider has issues the company relies on the others. Multi-clouds provide resilience.

4. Small business wanting low cost: Public cloud. A public cloud is offered over the internet, shared among multiple organizations and managed by a third-party provider such as AWS; businesses of all sizes use it without managing physical hardware. Public clouds are cost-effective but less secure.

book_ref.quote: while keeping critical data secure in the private cloud

rows: Cheap everyday work + secure critical data
Must not depend on one provider
Low-cost resources, no hardware to manage

blocks.prompt: 6 Cloud computing has revolutionized how data is managed, processed and stored. (i) How does the cloud help organizations? (ii) Explain three applications of cloud computing with examples. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Cloud computing's applications span various sectors, offering scalable and cost-effective solutions that enhance efficiency and innovation. It supports hosting websites, running applications, data storage and collaboration. By leveraging the cloud, organizations can streamline operations, reduce IT costs and rapidly respond to changing demands.

(ii) 1. Data storage: cloud storage lets users save data on remote servers rather than on local devices, so data can be accessed from anywhere and shared with others. Example: Google Drive and Dropbox let users store and share files online; businesses keep backups in cloud storage so data is safe from local hardware failures.

2. Web hosting and content delivery: cloud computing provides the infrastructure to host websites and deliver content efficiently to users around the world. Example: AWS and Microsoft Azure offer web hosting so businesses run their websites on cloud servers; content delivery networks (CDNs) such as Cloudflare deliver content quickly by caching it on servers close to the end-users.

3. Machine learning and AI in the cloud: the cloud offers powerful tools for developing and running machine learning models and AI applications. Example: Google Cloud AI and AWS SageMaker are platforms for building, training and deploying ML models, so data scientists and developers create AI solutions without extensive local computing resources.

book_ref.quote: Its diverse applications span various sectors, offering scalable and cost-effective solutions

blocks.prompt: 7 Cloud computing brings implications that must be considered. Explain the four implications given in the book: data security; scalability and resource management; cost considerations; compliance and regulatory issues. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
1. Data security: security is a significant concern because storing sensitive data on remote servers introduces risks such as data breaches and loss. Challenges: cloud providers implement robust security measures, but users must also protect their data; data breaches, unauthorized access and loss of data can occur. Measures: users should use encryption and strong authentication methods and regularly review their security policies; providers often offer tools to help manage and secure data.

2. Scalability and resource management: resources can be adjusted according to demand; cloud services can automatically scale up or down, e.g. adding servers at peak times and reducing them when demand decreases. Effective resource management (monitoring resource usage and optimizing performance) is essential to avoid unnecessary costs and ensure optimal performance.

3. Cost considerations: cloud computing can be cost-effective but needs careful financial management, because users pay for what they use and costs can quickly add up if not monitored. To manage costs, users should regularly review their usage and spending, optimize resource allocation and use pricing plans that fit their needs.

4. Compliance and regulatory issues: organizations must ensure their use of cloud services complies with legal and regulatory requirements, which can vary by region and industry. They must adhere to regulations on data privacy, security and industry-specific standards; cloud providers often offer tools and features to help meet these requirements.

book_ref.quote: While cloud computing offers numerous benefits, it also brings various implications

blocks.prompt: 8 Blockchain can be pictured as a shared digital notebook. (i) Define blockchain and describe the notebook picture. (ii) Explain its three special features: transparency, security and decentralization. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Blockchain is a secure and transparent way for people to share and keep track of information without needing to rely on one person or company to keep it safe; it enables secure and transparent transactions through a distributed ledger system.
Notebook picture: a group of friends keeps track of who owes whom money. Instead of writing it on a piece of paper that one person keeps, they all write it in a notebook of which everyone has a copy. Every time someone makes a change, like paying back money, it is recorded in all the notebooks at the same time. This digital notebook is the blockchain (Figure 6.2).

(ii) 1. Transparency: everyone in the group can see what is written in the notebook, so it is hard for anyone to cheat or change the information without others noticing.

2. Security: once something is written in the notebook, it is almost impossible to erase or change it, because it is protected by a special kind of math called cryptography, which locks the information in place.

3. Decentralization: there is no single person or computer in charge of the notebook. Everyone has an equal copy, and changes are only made when the majority agree, making it fair and trustworthy.

book_ref.quote: In simple terms, blockchain is a secure and transparent way for people to share and keep track of information

blocks.prompt: 9 Blockchain technology is built on core principles that ensure its functionality and security. Explain decentralization, immutability and consensus mechanisms, naming two consensus mechanisms. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
1. Decentralization: unlike traditional databases that are controlled by a central authority, a blockchain is maintained by a network of computers (nodes) that work together to validate and record transactions. This decentralized nature reduces the risk of a single point of failure and enhances security.

2. Immutability: once a block is added to the blockchain, it cannot be altered or deleted. This ensures that the transaction history is permanent and tamper-proof, giving a reliable and unchangeable record of all transactions.

3. Consensus mechanisms: blockchain networks use consensus mechanisms to agree on the validity of transactions before a new block is added to the chain. Agreement of a sufficient majority of the network is needed, not of every node: in Proof of Work the majority of computing power decides, and in Proof of Stake a majority (often two thirds) of the stake; a new block is added even if some nodes are offline or dishonest.
Two common consensus mechanisms: Proof of Work (PoW) and Proof of Stake (PoS).

book_ref.quote: Blockchain technology is built on several core principles that ensure its functionality and security

blocks.prompt: 10 A blockchain system is made of key components and runs on a peer-to-peer network. (i) Explain the components: node, ledger, block, transaction and blockchain protocol. (ii) What is a peer-to-peer network? Explain it with the book's file-sharing example. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) 1. Node: a computer that participates in the blockchain network. Each node maintains a copy of the blockchain and helps validate transactions and blocks.
2. Ledger: the digital record of all transactions that have occurred on the blockchain. It is distributed across all nodes, so everyone in the network has access to the same information.
3. Block: a collection of transactions bundled together. Each block contains a unique identifier (hash), a reference to the previous block (parent hash) and a list of transactions.
4. Transaction: an individual entry in the blockchain; it represents the transfer of assets or information between participants in the network.
5. Blockchain protocol: defines the rules and procedures for how transactions are validated, how blocks are added to the chain and how consensus is achieved; it ensures the integrity and security of the network.

(ii) A peer-to-peer (P2P) network is a system where computers, called nodes, communicate and share resources directly with each other without relying on a central server. Each node can act as both a client and a server, which makes the network more robust and decentralized.
Example: in a file-sharing network, users download files directly from each other's computers rather than from a single central server. This is faster and more efficient because multiple users can share parts of the file simultaneously.

book_ref.quote: Several key components make up a blockchain system

blocks.prompt: 11 Blockchain has a wide range of applications beyond cryptocurrency. Explain four use cases of blockchain technology given in the book. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
1. Cryptocurrencies: blockchain is the underlying technology for cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum. It enables secure, decentralised digital transactions without the need for intermediaries.

2. Supply chain management: blockchain is used to track and verify the movement of goods through the supply chain. This transparency helps prevent fraud, reduce errors and ensure the authenticity of products.

3. Healthcare: blockchain can securely store patient records, manage medical data and ensure that only authorised individuals have access to sensitive information.

4. Voting systems: blockchain can be used to create secure and transparent voting systems, ensuring that votes are accurately recorded and counted and reducing the risk of election fraud.

Blockchain is often compared to a digital ledger that everyone in the network can see and agree upon; once a page is added it cannot be changed, so everyone has the same record of events.

blocks.prompt: 12 Cryptocurrencies and smart contracts have changed digital finance. (i) Explain the role of cryptocurrencies in the digital economy. (ii) What are smart contracts? Explain them with the book's insurance example, and give their benefits and challenges. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Role of cryptocurrencies: cryptocurrencies are digital currencies that work without traditional banks, allowing direct transactions between people worldwide. They offer a secure and decentralized way to exchange money: unlike traditional money issued by banks, they use blockchain technology to keep transactions safe and transparent, recorded in a way that cannot be changed, without middlemen. Cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum let people send money quickly and cheaply, even across borders, and help people without access to traditional banking services take part in the global economy. Transactions are protected by cryptography.

(ii) Smart contracts are digital agreements that automatically carry out the terms written into them when specific conditions are met. They run on blockchain technology, removing the need for intermediaries and reducing the risk of errors and fraud. Platforms like Ethereum let developers create decentralized applications (DApps) using smart contracts; they are used in finance, supply chain management, real estate and insurance.
Example: an insurance smart contract can automatically pay out if a flight is delayed, based on pre-set conditions.
Benefits: transparency, because everyone involved can see the contract's terms; security, because the contract execution is guaranteed by the blockchain.
Challenges: the need for error-free code, and legal systems to resolve disputes related to these contracts.

book_ref.quote: These technologies together provide secure, transparent, and efficient ways to handle financial transactions and agreements

blocks.prompt: 13 Blockchain changes how products and certificates are verified. (i) Explain how blockchain tracks the origin of a product through the supply chain (Figure 6.3). (ii) Compare manual verification of academic certificates with blockchain-based verification. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Blockchain offers a transparent and secure way to track the origin and journey of products through the supply chain. Every transaction is recorded on a decentralized ledger, so each step from the raw material supplier to the final customer is traceable and immutable.
Figure 6.3 (origin of chocolate) shows the entities: suppliers, manufacturers, fabricators, intermediaries, retailers and customers. When a supplier delivers raw materials to a manufacturer, a record is created and added to the blockchain. This continues at each stage, with the fabricator, intermediary and retailer all adding to a transparent and verifiable history. Finally, the customer can access this data to confirm the product's origin and check that it meets the expected standards.
This traceability helps in verifying the authenticity of products, ensuring quality and identifying the source of any issues.

(ii) Traditionally, a request is submitted to the issuing authority, which verifies the certificate manually. With blockchain, the issuing authority (e.g. BISE) records certificate details on a decentralized ledger, and anyone can verify them by checking the blockchain.

book_ref.quote: In Figure 6.3, the connections between different entities in a supply chain are illustrated

blocks.prompt: 14 Data security in blockchain can be understood through the example of sending a secure letter. Define data security in blockchain and explain its four techniques using this example. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
Definition: data security in blockchain ensures that information stored in a blockchain is protected from unauthorized access, tampering or loss. In the example, you want to send a letter with important information to a friend so that no one else can read or change it on the way.

1. Sealing the letter (Encryption): you place the letter in a special envelope that only your friend can open. In blockchain, encryption turns the data into a code that only the intended recipient (or those with the right key) can understand (Figure 6.5). Encryption protects the data, so only those with permission can read it.

2. Signing the letter (Digital signature): you sign the envelope with your unique signature, known to your friend, so they are sure it came from you and hasn't been altered. A digital signature ensures that the data comes from a legitimate source and hasn't been tampered with.

3. Sending through a trusted system (Blockchain network): you use a secure delivery service where every step is recorded; any attempt to change the route or tamper with the letter is detected and rejected. In blockchain, each piece of data is recorded in a block and any change to it is noticed by the network.

4. Multiple copies of the letter (Decentralization): you send copies through different trusted services to multiple locations, so even if one is lost, others arrive. In blockchain, data is stored across multiple computers (nodes), so even if one is compromised the data remains safe and it is very hard for hackers to attack or change it.

By combining these techniques, blockchain provides a very secure way to store and transfer data.

book_ref.quote: By combining these techniques, blockchain provides a very secure way to store and transfer data

rows: Sealing the letter in a special envelope
Trusted delivery service that records every step
